intro: Real programs fail karte hain: file missing ho sakti hai, JSON kharab ho sakta hai, conversion fail ho sakta hai. Is section me exceptions ko sahi jagah pakadna, files safely read/write karna aur modules import karke code reuse karna practice hota hai.
theory: try/except sirf us code ko wrap karta hai jahan failure expected hai; poora function wrap karna bugs chhupa deta hai. Specific exception pakdo, bare `except:` nahi.
else tab chalta hai jab try bina exception ke poora ho; finally har haal me chalta hai — file close ya lock release ke liye.
`raise` se exception dobara throw hoti hai; custom exception class domain error ko naam deti hai. `raise ... from None` confusing chained traceback hata deta hai.
File ke liye `with open(...)` use karo — error par bhi file close hoti hai. Encoding explicitly do (`encoding="utf-8"`), warna platform default bharosa nahi.
Module import karne se code reuse hota hai: `import math`, `from pathlib import Path`, `import json`. Har module ka apna namespace hota hai, isliye naam collision kam hote hain.
syntax:
from pathlib import Path
import json

path = Path("data.json")
path.write_text(json.dumps({"ok": True}), encoding="utf-8")
print(json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))

examples.code:
import json

payload = {'name': 'Asha', 'scores': [91, 85]}
text = json.dumps(payload)
restored = json.loads(text)
print(text)
print(restored['name'], restored['scores'])
explain: json.dumps text banata hai aur loads usse wapas Python object me laata hai.
Output ko print se verify karo.
Ye Exceptions, Files & Modules ka basic building block hai.

examples.code:
from pathlib import Path

path = Path('reports') / 'daily.csv'
print(path.name, path.stem, path.suffix)
print(path.parent)
explain: Path objects path join aur parts ko readable aur cross-platform banate hain.
Ek step aur jodne se behaviour kaise badalta hai, dekho.
Input badal kar edge case test karo.

examples.code:
import csv
import io

raw = 'name,score\nAsha,91\nRavi,not-a-number\nMeera,85\n'
rows, skipped = [], 0

for row in csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(raw)):
    try:
        rows.append((row['name'], int(row['score'])))
    except ValueError:
        skipped += 1

print('valid:', rows)
print('skipped:', skipped)
explain: csv.DictReader + per-row try/except se ek bad row poore import ko fail nahi karti.
Ye snippet end-to-end flow dikhata hai.
Output ko project/interview me evidence ki tarah use karo.

realWorld: Config/JSON load karte waqt missing file aur invalid JSON do alag failures hain — dono ko alag message dena operator ka time bachata hai.
ETL me ek bad row poore batch ko fail na kare, isliye per-row parse ko try/except me rakha jata hai aur skipped count report hota hai.
Temp files aur reports likhte waqt `with` + explicit encoding use karna Windows/Linux dono par same behaviour deta hai.

interview.q: Bare `except:` kyun avoid karna chahiye?
interview.a: Wo KeyboardInterrupt aur system exits bhi pakad leta hai, bugs chhupa deta hai aur debugging mushkil banata hai. Specific exception types pakdo.

interview.q: else aur finally ka role kya hai?
interview.a: else try ke successful completion par chalta hai, isliye success-only code try ke andar nahi rakhna padta. finally har case me chalta hai — cleanup ke liye.

interview.q: File handling me with kyun zaroori hai?
interview.a: with context manager error par bhi file close karta hai. Manual open ke saath exception aane par descriptor leak ho sakta hai.

interview.q: Custom exception kab banate hain?
interview.a: Jab caller ko domain error ko alag handle karna ho. Standard exception reuse karna theek hai jab semantics match karein; custom class tab jab library-specific error contract chahiye.

debugging.why: Naam ki spelling galat hai; Python namespace me wo naam nahi milta. Ye Exceptions, Files & Modules ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.lesson: NameError typo ya missing assignment batata hai.

debugging.error: Logic error — sort() None return karta hai, list print nahi hoti
debugging.why: sort() in-place hai aur None deta hai, isliye print None dikhata hai. Ye Exceptions, Files & Modules ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: sorted() use karo ya pehle sort phir list print karo.
debugging.lesson: Mutating methods ka return value None hota hai — usse assign/print mat karo.

debugging.broken:
prices = [100, 200]
total = 0
for p in prices:
    total = p
print(total)
debugging.error: Logic error — total 200 aata hai, sum 300 hona chahiye
debugging.why: Assignment purani value replace karta hai; accumulator chahiye. Ye Exceptions, Files & Modules ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: total += p use karo ya sum(prices).
debugging.correct:
prices = [100, 200]
total = 0
for p in prices:
    total += p
print(total)
debugging.lesson: Logic bugs exception nahi dete — chhote sample par expected value likho.

debugging.error: Logic error — pehla do items chahiye the, sirf pehla aaya
debugging.why: Slice ka end exclusive hota hai; 0:1 sirf index 0 deta hai. Ye Exceptions, Files & Modules ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.lesson: Slice boundaries exclusive hoti hain — range jaisa hi rule.
